method_note: Source-level reading only (no lake build, no kernel check). Inventory by regex over declaration keywords; matching by (a) explicit label citations in comments/docstrings, (b) declaration names, (c) content against the merged ledger hypotheses/conclusions, with the statements of the cited declarations read from source. "FORMALIZED" means one or more Lean declarations state the same mathematical content (possibly in a different generality or packaging); it is not a claim that the Lean proof follows the paper's proof, nor that the Lean statement's hypotheses are identical. In the map, a lean entry whose name begins with "(module: ...)" and whose line is 1 refers to a whole module (its header docstring describes the content) rather than to one declaration; entries with a real line number point at the declaration read from source.

lean_inventory.organisation: Flat directory NavierStokes/ with 573 modules named by mathematical object or construction stage (e.g. AxisContraction, OutgoingTail, TrueConeLoop, CorrectionStep, SlowBorelBase, SpatialLocalization) plus NavierStokes/R3/ (70 modules: whole-space pressure recovery, Riesz/heat-kernel commutator, finite-energy comparison) and the Comparator* glue. No file or section is named after a paper section. Euler/ (a different paper) and ComparatorChallenges/ (reference statements) were ignored.
lean_inventory.citation_style: 54 label citations in module headers/docstrings, all to a "candidate manuscript"/"supplied manuscript"/"the manuscript" whose numbering does NOT match the 79-statement paper except for "Theorem 1.1" (and "Part II, Theorem 1.1" in R3/ProblemStatement): e.g. Lean cites Lemma 3.3/3.5/3.6/3.7 (= paper Lemma 4.3/4.5/4.7/A.2), Proposition 3.2 (= 4.2), Lemma 4.4 (= A.6), Proposition 5.1/Lemma 5.2 (= B.2/B.4), Lemma 6.1/Proposition 6.2 (= C.1/C.2), Definition 8.1, Lemma 8.3/8.4/8.5/8.7/8.8 (= 6.1/7.1/7.4/7.5/7.7), Lemma 9.2, Proposition 9.3, Proposition 10.3 (= 9.6), Lemma 11.2-11.5 and Proposition 11.4/11.7 (= Section 10 / 5.4), Proposition A.2/A.4, Appendix A.3, Remark 8.6, sections 4.4, 4.6, 8.1, 8.2, 8.3, 10.2, 11. Equation numbers are cited as small integers "(3)-(5)", "(6)-(9)", "(11)", "(21)", "(22)", "(24)"-"(27)", "(29)", "(32)"-"(34)", not the paper's (x.y) numbering. Hence label matching was only a hint; every verdict rests on content.

map.note: Proved in the Clay-(C) form: for every nu>0 there are u0=0 and a smooth compactly supported force with no global smooth finite-energy solution; the constructed fields (R3CompactCandidate.Properties: smooth on [0,1)xR^3, compact spatial support of u,p,f, zero datum, exact NS at viscosity one, SpeedUnboundedAtOne) are the paper's (u,p,f) at nu=1 and are rescaled in the bridge. The literal target `NavierStokesR3.ProblemStatement.breakdownStatement` (with an explicit energy_bounded field, cited as "Part II, Theorem 1.1") is declared as a Prop but never proved as written; the energy bound is derived from compact support (R3/CompactComparisonBounds.uniformFiniteEnergy_of_compact_slab). The rate (10.21) is not part of the Lean conclusion (only unbounded speed).

No single Lean theorem states the local-field theorem on Omega_*. Its four items are present but distributed and repackaged: (i) potential + direct angular field summed with cutoffs (MixedCandidateAssembly, SolenoidalDiagonal); (ii) one-sided endpoint jets via JointResidualLimits/SpacetimeEndpoint; (iii) all-jet flat residual (DiagonalResidual) and exact heat exterior (BaseExterior/ModulatedExterior with the gamma-integral heat profile); (iv) only divergence of the axis velocity (Tendsto atTop), not the rate tau^{-A}(e_0+O(tau^{2h})). route_differences: (1) Order of results: the Lean project constructs a PERIODIC viscosity-one candidate first (ActualCandidateAssembly.selected_candidate proving ProblemStatement.candidateStatement) and derives alternative (D) from periodic uniqueness/maximal lifespan; the whole-space alternative (C) is then obtained by extracting the compactly supported fields behind the periodisation (R3CompactCandidate.of_localized_fields) and applying whole-space finite-energy uniqueness. The paper proves Theorem 1.1 on R^3 first and obtains Corollary 10.6 by rescaling into the fundamental cube and periodising. (2) There is no Lean counterpart of the local-field theorem (Theorem 3.1) on Omega_* as a separate statement: MixedCandidateAssembly.candidate_of_finite_stages goes from finite correction stages directly to CandidateProperties, folding Proposition 9.9, Proposition 10.1 (cut potential before curl, direct angular field cut separately, time switch), Lemma 10.2 (joint jet limits) and Lemma 10.3 (Borel extension) into one assembly; the inner growth (3.6)/(10.21) is used only as unbounded speed (Tendsto atTop), not as an asymptotic rate. (3) Viscosity is fixed to one throughout the construction and restored by the scaling in ComparatorBridge (force nu^2 f(nu t, x)), essentially the paper's (10.22). (4) Lemma 10.5 (weak-strong uniqueness without growth assumptions on the competitor's pressure) is proved by a full pressure-recovery/Riesz-commutator argument (NavierStokes/R3/) rather than the paper's short energy argument. (5) The Lean cites a "candidate manuscript" with different numbering (Part I periodic with sections 3-11 and Appendix A; "Part II" whole space), so the Lean was written against an earlier draft; intermediate statements are organised by construction stage (nominal profile Witness structures, correction-cycle Invariant records, weighted classes on StripData) rather than by the paper's lemma list, and many paper lemmas correspond to several Lean declarations (see match_form).
gate_answer: Measured at source level (no build), the OpenAI Lean project (34,605 declarations in 644 files, no sorry, no axiom declarations) contains counterparts for all 79 numbered statements: 74 are FORMALIZED (a Lean declaration, or a small set of them, states the same mathematical content; 27 by a single declaration, 47 distributed over several) and 5 are PARTIAL (Theorem 3.1, whose four items appear separately and whose growth rate is weakened to unbounded speed; Definition 3.3, a parameter-ordering convention realised only by quantifier order; Lemma 4.4, whose general Lipschitz estimate appears only in the special forms used; Corollary 7.3 and Lemma 9.7, which are realised structurally by a single common domain rather than stated). None is ABSENT or STATED-ONLY. The top-level content of Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 10.6 is proved in the Clay (C)/(D) forms, but the Lean route differs: periodic candidate first, whole-space fields extracted afterwards, and the local-field theorem merged into the final assembly. The Lean comments cite a differently numbered draft, so this mapping rests on content, and "FORMALIZED" is not a kernel check nor a claim that the Lean proofs follow the paper's proofs.
